title: create-objectstack: blank template Dockerfile uses `:latest` while its own comment says to pin the CLI version
body:
Found while implementing #8961 (PR #9016). Out of that card's scope — its file surface was `docker/README.md` only, and the card explicitly said not to touch this file — so filing rather than fixing.

## The defect

`packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/Dockerfile:26` (line numbers as of `origin/main` at the time of filing — re-derive before fixing):

```dockerfile
# ── Runtime: the official ObjectStack runtime image ──────────────────
# Ships Node + @objectstack/cli with `os start`, a non-root user, the
# /api/v1/health HEALTHCHECK, and OS_ARTIFACT_PATH/OS_PORT preset (port 8080)
# — see docker/README.md in the framework repo. Pin the tag to the
# @objectstack/cli version in your package.json so the runtime matches the
# CLI that built the artifact.
FROM ghcr.io/objectstack-ai/objectstack:latest
```

The comment immediately above the `FROM` line instructs the reader to "Pin the tag to the `@objectstack/cli` version in your package.json" — but the line itself uses `:latest`, the opposite of what the comment says. This template is scaffolded once per app via `npx create-objectstack`, so every newly scaffolded app ships with this self-contradiction baked in from day one: the generated Dockerfile silently drifts to whatever runtime image is newest at each rebuild, unrelated to the `@objectstack/cli` version actually pinned in the generated `package.json` — the opposite of what the adjacent comment promises the reader.

## Why this matters

`docker/README.md`'s own tag table documents `X.Y.Z` as "pin this in production" and scopes `latest` to "quick starts only." A scaffolded production app template landing on `:latest` contradicts both that guidance and its own inline comment.

## Suggested fix

Either:
- Change the `FROM` line to reference the CLI version resolved at scaffold time (matching the version written into the generated `package.json`), so the comment and the line agree; or
- If `:latest` is deliberate for quick-start ergonomics, update the comment to stop instructing the reader to pin, since scaffolded output currently doesn't practice what it preaches.

Related: #8961, PR #9016 (docker/README.md's own three occurrences of this same "example image tag" concern, on the concrete-version side of it).
